notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out or flagged: Amwal Al Ghad's Wednesday flow figures, which are in billions and disagree with Youm7 (foreign institutions net buy EGP 338.7 mn); Youm7 gives the market-cap gain as EGP 99 mn in one place, so only the EGP 3.989 tn level is used; turnover differs between Youm7 (EGP 11.2 bn) and EnterpriseAM (EGP 9 bn, likely EGX30 only); reports that US strikes could begin after the midterms; Iran's claim that four tankers were destroyed by mines; October's net international reserves (not yet published); the budget's oil-price assumption; Egypt's October inflation figure.

items: Democrats win both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, with CNBC projecting at least 245 House seats and at least 51 in the Senate → a divided Washington constrains Trump's agenda for the rest of his term, including war spending, as talks with Iran continue.

EGX30 rebounds 1.76% to 49,255.66 on Tuesday, ending a four-session fall, as 180 stocks rise and foreigners net buy about EGP 130 mn → a firmer pound and lower oil bring back foreign buyers; developers and Eastern Company lead while fertiliser names fall.

Gas supplies to fertilizer plants are cut 20% while Egyptian urea sells at $535 a ton, about 17% above September → LNG cargoes now cost over $100 mn each, so the state rations gas; Abu Qir confirms the cut and falls 3.59%.

Brent settles 1% lower at $103.60, its lowest close since 7 October, as traders weigh US-Iran talks → Iran calls the US reply unconvincing, but Qatar expects both sides' feedback within 36 hours; lower oil eases Egypt's import bill.

The government weighs selling a large EgyptAlum stake on the EGX before year-end, after Banque du Caire raised $658 mn → the state targets $1.5 bn of offerings this year; a new listing would add depth for brokers and investors.

Brent falls 7.6% to $104.77 on Monday, its biggest drop in three months, after Iran's supreme leader approves talks and Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz in two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound, though a US strike on Qeshm Island overnight lifts Brent 0.5% in Asia.

The pound strengthens to EGP 55.51 per dollar at the CBE on Monday from 56.12 after the hike, and major banks quote 55.49 → the 100 bp hike and falling oil ease demand for dollars; a firmer pound helps importers and foreign holders of local debt.

EGX30 slips 0.70% to 48,403.14 while the EGX70 and EGX100 fall more than 2.2% and 197 stocks decline against 31 → foreigners net sell EGP 138.1 mn and Banque du Caire absorbs 21% of turnover, leaving little cash for small caps.

Banque du Caire closes its first session at EGP 5.31, up 0.19% on the EGP 5.30 offer, after touching EGP 5.68 → pricing at fair value leaves little first-day gain; the Treasury takes up to half the EGP 36.37 bn proceeds to ease debt.

Egypt's non-oil PMI stays at 47.2 in October, below a 48 forecast and its tenth straight month below 50 → output and new orders fall at the fastest pace in four months and input costs rise at a five-month high.

EGX30 falls 1.72% to 48,744.01 in the first session after the hike, with 148 stocks down and only 63 up as Palm Hills drops 7% → higher rates hit developers and consumer lenders while foreign and Arab investors sell; turnover of EGP 7.2 bn is 35% below its 90-day average.

Banque du Caire starts trading today as BQDC at an offer price of EGP 5.30, after a record EGP 205.8 bn of private-placement orders → the debut tests demand in a falling market; retail holders can sell back at EGP 5.30 for 30 days through CI Capital.

The state borrows about EGP 4.3 tn at home in July to October, almost all to refinance, and a finance official says the hike adds EGP 150 bn to the bill → short-dated debt reprices fast, so the 100 bp move feeds straight into the budget; the first post-hike 364-day bill sells at 26.076%.

Brent falls about 3.2% to $109.75 early Monday after Iran says a Qatari-brokered plan could reopen Hormuz within two days → a lower oil price eases Egypt's import bill, but Trump still talks of hitting one or two more targets after Tuesday's midterms.

AMOC reports quarterly sales up 41% to EGP 43.2 bn and net profit up 154% to EGP 3.475 bn → high oil prices and refining margins lift results; the stock rises 2.21% on Sunday against a falling market.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Iran says Hormuz stays shut and there are no nuclear talks until the US meets its demands, as one report says US strikes could come as early as 4 November → the risk of a wider war after the midterms keeps oil, shipping and regional risk premiums high as the EGX reopens.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The pound holds at EGP 56.12 per dollar at the CBE as banks open Sunday at 56.04–56.19 to sell, the first quotes after the hike → the hike has not yet moved the pound, so today's EGX session tests how equities price higher rates.

Brent's expiring December contract settles 2.4% higher at $117.64 on Friday, a six-month high, after the first limpet-mine strike on a tanker in Hormuz since February → traders brace for a US strike on Iran after Tuesday's midterms, and Brent ends October up 13.6%, widening Egypt's fuel bill.

Saudi Arabia agrees to keep a $5.3 bn deposit at the CBE for another year instead of taking it back at end-October, banking sources say → the renewal removes a large maturity just as foreign money leaves Egyptian debt; no official statement confirms it yet.

The first T-bill auction after the hike sets the 364-day yield at 26.076%, up from 25.912% on 27 October, and the state takes EGP 78.84 bn of a EGP 110 bn target → the CBE's 100 bp move is passing into bill yields, which supports bank income and the carry trade but raises the state's borrowing cost.

The S&P 500 falls 1.8% and the Nasdaq 2.9% on Friday after Intel's outlook, while gold drops 3.52% to $3,879.90 → a risk-off week end and forced selling of metals weigh on sentiment toward emerging markets before the EGX reopens.

Qatari mediators in Tehran deliver a Vance letter proposing a new diplomatic process, with a meeting possible within a week in Doha or Istanbul → talks offer a path away from escalation, but reports say Trump has told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the midterms.

stories.h: Brent falls 8.7% below $95 as Vance blames the midterm loss on the Iran war
stories.what: Brent settles at $94.62, down 8.7%, and WTI at $88.12, down 8.3%; oil futures are down more than 14% this week. Vance writes that "The reason we lost is the war," and Trump tells the Financial Times he has no immediate plans to strike Iran. JPMorgan estimates the global oil surplus at 1.4 mn bpd in October, and Middle East exports have recovered to about 20.7 mn bpd from 9.8 mn in March, Oilprice.com reports.
stories.why: Democrats' control of Congress is read as raising pressure to end the war, possibly through war funding; some analysts warn the sell-off may be overdone.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel and LNG import bill, the pound, inflation and Gulf budgets.
stories.eg: Each fall in crude lowers the dollar cost of Egypt's energy imports and the subsidy bill.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers, consumer and energy users; bearish for oil-linked AMOC.

key.l: CBE sell rate, EGP per USD, Wed 4 Nov

stories.h: Pound gains 65 piasters in a day to 54.77 per dollar
stories.what: The CBE's closing rate on Wednesday is 54.63 buy and 54.77 sell, down 65 piasters from the session's opening level of 55.28 and 55.42, Egyin reports. National Bank of Egypt quotes 54.67 and 54.77, and Banque Misr 54.80 and 54.90. Cairo Mubasher confirms the CBE's 54.77 closing rate.
stories.why: Falling oil prices and the CBE's 100 bp hike ease dollar demand; neither source gives a single cause.
stories.aff: Import costs, inflation, foreign holders of local debt and companies with dollar debt.
stories.eg: A stronger pound lowers the cost of imported fuel, wheat and inputs.
stories.egx: Bullish for importers and foreign-held blue chips; mildly bearish for exporters' pound revenue.

stories.h: EGX30 jumps 2.83% back above 50,000 as foreign institutions buy
stories.what: The EGX30 closes Wednesday at 50,650.18, up 2.83%; the EGX70 rises 3.02% and the EGX100 2.98%. 197 stocks rise and 16 fall, and market cap reaches EGP 3.989 tn. Rameda (+7.0%), Ibnsina (+6.9%) and Edita (+6.6%) lead, while AMOC (-1.3%) falls. Foreign institutions net buy EGP 338.7 mn and Egyptian institutions net sell EGP 247.8 mn.
stories.why: Peace hopes, a sharp fall in oil and a stronger pound coincide with the foreign buying; none of the sources gives a single cause.
stories.aff: Foreign-held blue chips, consumer and pharma names, and small caps.
stories.eg: EnterpriseAM puts the EGX30 down 4.43% in October, when foreigners net sold EGP 2.3 bn of stocks.
stories.egx: Bullish across the market; oil-linked AMOC lags.

key.l: Qatar's window for feedback on its proposal

stories.h: Iran calls the US reply unconvincing as Qatar keeps talks alive
stories.what: Mohsen Rezaei says Washington's response to Iran's seven demands is not convincing; Iran offers to reopen Hormuz over two days if the US lifts sanctions and its naval blockade. Trump confirms a "minor" strike on an anti-aircraft site on Qeshm Island, and the IRGC claims four tankers hit mines. Iran's chief negotiator says the midterms show Americans reject the war, and China calls avoiding renewed conflict a top priority.
stories.why: Both sides keep talking through Qatari, Pakistani and Saudi mediators while attacks on shipping continue.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping, regional risk premiums and Suez traffic.
stories.eg: A deal would ease Egypt's energy costs and help a Suez recovery.
stories.egx: Neutral pending a deal; the market is pricing in de-escalation.

key.l: Banque du Caire stake held by three foreign institutions

stories.h: EBRD, IFC and Helikon disclose about 6.9% each of Banque du Caire
stories.what: The EBRD (6.90%), Helikon Long Short Equity Fund (6.89%) and the IFC (6.89%) each buy about 1.05 bn shares of Banque du Caire at EGP 5.30, about EGP 16.7 bn in total. The purchases, executed on 29 October through CI Capital's brokerage, are disclosed in filings to the EGX.
stories.why: The investors bought as cornerstones in the 45% offering.
stories.aff: BQDC's free float, foreign ownership of state banks and the privatisation programme.
stories.eg: Large development-bank and fund holders support confidence in state asset sales.
stories.egx: Bullish for sentiment toward BQDC and future state listings.

key.l: development fee waived on zone-made phones sold locally

stories.h: Government waives the 5% fee on phones made in zones and sold locally
stories.what: The finance ministry drops the 5% development fee on handsets that factories in economic and investment zones sell in Egypt, giving up part of the EGP 1.9 bn the budget expected from the fee. Output is about 10.5 mn handsets from 15 global brands, and the target is 14–15 mn this year. Samsung, Oppo, Vivo and Xiaomi's assembler Al Safy are among the makers named.
stories.why: The government wants more local assembly investment and capacity in return.
stories.aff: Phone makers, electronics suppliers and the local handset market.
stories.eg: More local assembly cuts imports of finished devices and saves dollars.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for electronics and distribution; no large EGX name is directly named.

week.why: The first inflation print after the CBE's 100 bp hike; September urban inflation was 13.9%. CAPMAS usually publishes around the 9th or 10th.
